item.title: Boujloud: Morocco’s Most Controversial Tradition
item.description: Despite its deep roots in Amazigh culture, Boujloud remains one of Morocco’s most misunderstood traditions. Also known as Bilmawen, it is an Amazigh folk celebration held in the days following Eid al-Adha. Participants wear costumes made from animal skins and move through neighborhoods to the rhythm of drums. Supporters describe it as a centuries-old cultural expression rooted in North Africa’s Indigenous heritage, symbolizing renewal and communal celebration. Others find the imagery disturbing.
